412 pages of a thriller this month. 0 pages of Qur’an. 📖

Saturday night on a café terrace, chapter 31, the tea gone cold. Back home, on the top shelf: a green cover under the dust. First page — your name, in your mother’s handwriting. Ramadan 2019.

“Your Lord has not taken leave of you, [O Muhammad], nor has He detested [you].” (93:3)

The dust is yours. He never left.

Today, before Dhuhr: one page of Qur’an. Just one.

captions: Saturday, 9:40 p.m. The café terrace. Chapter 31.
Your tea went cold an hour ago. You didn’t notice.
Page after page. Then another chapter. Then another.
“Don’t spoil the ending,” you tell your friend.
11:20 p.m. Home. You put the book on the shelf.
Top shelf. A green cover under a layer of dust.
First page: your name. Your mother’s handwriting.
Ramadan 2019. The last date written beside it.
Sunday, 8:15 a.m. The library opens. You came early.
No phone. One page. Your finger under every word.
Then a second page. Slow. Stumbling. Yours.
The dust is gone. He never left.
